verdict.rationale: Klaviyo documents private API keys with API key scopes for all /api endpoints, and says scopes limit what third parties can access, including a Custom option to choose how much access to grant. That is first-party support for minting scoped credentials. However, the evidence never shows a read-only or analytics-only scope that withholds send or campaign-creation permissions, nor the steps an ops user follows to mint and hand off such a key. missing for 10: documented read-only/analytics-only scope that excludes send permissions, key-creation and revocation workflow details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can mint scoped or read-only API credentials so an agent or contractor can read analytics without the power to send

citations.quote: All `/api` endpoints use private API keys with API key scopes to authenticate requests.
Adding a scope helps you protect your and your customers’ data by limiting what third parties can access.
Custom Allows you to decide how much access to give the third party
